To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
high-affinity ECF-EGFR binding and EGFR-ErBB2 heterodimer formation are regulated by different molecular mechanisms.
the affinity of EDF binding and EGFR-ErBB2 heterodimer formation are regulated by different processes, which are independent of each other.

overexpression of a mutant form of dynamin that blocks clathrin-dependent internalization disrupts high-affinitity binding of EGF to the EGFR, while EGF-induced EGFR-Erb2 heterodimer formation and Erb2 phosphorylation remain unaffected.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms that regulate the affinity and the dimerization state of the EGFR and its role as an oncogene.
how endocytosis regulates EGF-EGF receptor interactions, which is important to understand the role of EGF in cell growth regulation.
the regulation of EGFR-Erb2 heterodimer formation and EGF binding to EGFR, and the role of protein kinases in this regulation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

high-affinity ECF binding to EGFR is disrupted in [K44A]-dynamin-overexpressing cells due to activation of a protein kinase, which phosphorylates a yet unidentified substrate, and that this kinase does not phosphorylate the EGFR.
the effect of overexpression of [ K44A]dynami n on EGF binding to EGFR is due to an activated protein kinase, which in turn phosphorylates an unidentified protein substrate.

the EGF-induced high-affinity binding to EGFR is dependent on clathrin-dependent receptor internalization, whereas the EGF-induced heterodimerization of EGFR with ErbB2 is independent of clathrin-dependent internalization.

overexpression of [k44A]dynami causes a disruption of the high affinity binding of EGF to the EGFR, but not to the ErbB2 receptor.
the EGF-induced EGFR-Erb B2 heterodimer formation is regulated independently of the EGF-induced high-affinity ECF-EGFR interaction.

high-affinity EFG-EGFR interaction is not essential for EGFR-Erb2 hetero-dimer formation, and that EGF-induced ErbB2 tyrosine phosphorylaiton is not influenced by overexpresssion of [K44]dynamin.
